question: What mechanisms drive re-entrant phase transitions in systems with paramagnetic ligands?
answer: Re-entrant phase transitions in systems with paramagnetic ligands are driven by a competition between magnetic and elastic contributions. In the case of the La(hfac)₃(pyDTDA)₂ complex, this phenomenon involves the rupture of pancake bonds between π-radicals, resulting in sequential structural phase transitions. The magnetic contribution arises from the singlet-triplet energy difference of the radical pairs forming the pancake bonds, while the elastic term reflects the flexibility of the lattice. The softness of the lattice allows the magnetic term to dominate over a specific temperature range, stabilizing a low-symmetry triclinic re-entrant phase. This behavior is further influenced by the modulation of lattice rigidity and the strength of pancake bonds.

### Task 1: Summarize the Purpose of the Paper  
The paper investigates π-π radical interactions and their role in supramolecular recognition, focusing on their ability to induce switchable structural and magnetic properties. By studying the La(hfac)₃(pyDTDA)₂ coordination complex, the authors observe rare re-entrant phase transitions driven by "pancake bonding" between π-radical ligands. The paper develops a theoretical model that explains this behavior and extends the findings to predict re-entrant phase transitions in other systems with low lattice rigidity.
